title: Cache regression alert tuning notes (hit-rate / eviction pressure / wasted prefill)
content:
Context
- Goal of alerts is to catch real cache regressions (runtime bugs, config changes, capacity/pressure issues, routing locality changes) without paging on expected workload shifts (diurnal + customer mix) or on telemetry pipeline issues.
- Signals in scope (new telemetry):
  - Prefix cache: hit-rate, reuse depth/tokens reused distribution.
  - KV cache: hit-rate, reuse effectiveness.
  - Evictions/pressure: eviction counts + reasons; memory pressure gauge(s).
  - “Wasted prefill”: prefill tokens that did not contribute to subsequent decode due to misses/evictions.
- This doc is SRE working notes for initial thresholds + anti-flap logic for the first rollout.

Definitions we’re alerting on (as of March sprint)
- Cache hit-rate (prefix + KV): defined per ADR. Important: avoid mixing “requests” vs “tokens”. We should prefer token-weighted hit-rate for cost impact.
- Wasted prefill rate: wasted_prefill_tokens / prefill_tokens (or wasted_prefill_tokens / total_tokens depending on availability). Use with care on short prompts.
- Eviction pressure: treat as correlated indicators:
  - eviction_rate (evictions/sec) AND
  - pressure_gauge (e.g., cache_mem_utilization or “eviction_pressure_index”) AND
  - rising wasted prefill.

Primary tuning principle
- Use multi-signal alerts with minimum traffic gating to reduce false positives.
- Prefer “ticket” alerts by default; page only when:
  1) sustained, material regression AND
  2) affects multiple routes/models/regions OR a high-tier workload AND
  3) not explained by telemetry gaps.

Where false positives come from (observed + expected)
1) Diurnal patterns / batch windows
- Overnight (US) tends to shift mix towards:
  - embeddings-heavy workloads (less cache reuse relevance)
  - scheduled batch summarization jobs (very long prompts; can stress cache memory)
  - multi-tenant “burstiness” in Hosted
- Result: hit-rate can drift even if nothing is broken.

2) Workload mix changes
- A single large tenant or new route rolling out can shift global aggregates.
- Long-prompt distributions change hit-rate mechanically:
  - more unique prompts -> lower hit-rate
  - more repeated system prompts / canonicalization -> higher hit-rate
- Must slice by request-shape buckets (prompt length bins) to understand if it’s a true regression.

3) Model/version rollouts
- Version mismatch misses can tank hit-rate even if cache is “working”. (See SUP-3912 root cause.)
- Alert should incorporate “miss_reason=version_mismatch” as a classifier rather than paging on the total dip.

4) Region imbalance / routing locality changes
- If routing shifts traffic between regions/POPs, locality drops -> hit-rate drops.
- Should cross-check “region” and “deployment_mode” splits before declaring incident.

5) Telemetry pipeline gaps / label drops
- If ingestion cardinality guards drop labels (SUP-3927) or pipeline is backpressured, dashboards show zeros.
- Must have separate alert for “telemetry missing / dropped series” to avoid paging for a phantom regression.

Metric selection notes (what we should and should not alert on)
- Do NOT page on raw hit-rate by itself. Too mix-sensitive.
- Prefer derived/regression-style alerts:
  - “Hit-rate drop relative to trailing baseline, within same request-shape bucket”
  - “Wasted prefill spike + eviction pressure increase”
  - “Miss_reason skew shift (capacity/ttl_expired/policy_disabled/version_mismatch/hash_mismatch)”
- Use token-weighted ratios where possible (better aligns to cost and user impact).

Traffic gating / minimum volume
- Any ratio alert must be gated by:
  - min_prefill_tokens (or min_requests) over window
  - AND min_unique_series count check to avoid single-route noise
- Proposed default gates (initial):
  - Hosted: >= 5e6 prefill tokens / 15m per region+model family (or >= 50k requests if tokens not available)
  - Dedicated: >= 5e5 prefill tokens / 15m per deployment
  - Private: no paging by default; ticket alerts only unless explicitly opted-in by customer SLO contract.

Baselines: how to account for diurnal patterns
Option A (preferred): time-of-week baseline
- Compare current value to same hour-of-week median over trailing 2–3 weeks.
- Pros: strong diurnal + weekday handling.
- Cons: needs enough history; rollout starts with limited data.

Option B (bootstrapping): trailing median baseline
- Compare current 30m value to trailing 24h median for same slice (model family + region + prompt bucket).
- Pros: works immediately.
- Cons: can miss slow regressions or follow the regression.

Practical rollout plan
- Week 1 after rollout: use Option B with conservative thresholds and “ticket-only” defaults.
- After 2–3 weeks of stable history: switch to Option A for “page candidate” alerts.

Proposed alert candidates (initial pass)

1) Cache telemetry missing / ingestion drop (PAGE)
- Symptom: sudden across-the-board near-zero cache metrics with stable request volume.
- Condition:
  - request_volume stable (±20%) AND
  - cache_hit_counters absent OR drop > 95% across > 70% of regions for >= 10m
- Action: page Telemetry oncall (Logan team) and SRE secondary.
- Notes:
  - This is the “don’t trust the ratios” gate. If this fires, suppress cache regression pages.

2) Eviction pressure spike (TICKET → PAGE if sustained)
- Condition (per region + model family + deployment_mode):
  - pressure_gauge > 0.85 for 15m AND
  - eviction_rate p95 over 15m > (trailing 24h median * 2) AND
  - wasted_prefill_rate increases by > 10 percentage points vs trailing baseline
- Default severity: ticket.
- Escalate to page if:
  - affects >= 2 regions OR >= 2 model families OR a tier-0 route allowlist
  - persists >= 30m
- Rationale: pressure alone happens with batchy long prompts; we page when it couples with wasted prefill (actual cost impact) and broad scope.

3) Hit-rate regression within prompt-length bucket (TICKET)
- Condition (per model family + region + prompt_len_bucket):
  - token_weighted_hit_rate drops by > 8 percentage points vs baseline for 30m
  - gated by min_prefill_tokens
- Exclusions:
  - ignore buckets with prompt_len_bucket < 256 tokens (too noisy, hit-rate saturates)
- Notes:
  - This is a triage alert meant to point to the bucket that moved.
  - Not a page until we add better “impact scoring”.

4) Miss reason shift classifiers (TICKET)
- Trigger when miss_reason distribution shifts materially:
  - version_mismatch share > 5% of misses and rising
  - policy_disabled share jumps (config change / route rollout)
  - capacity share spikes (capacity constrained / locality drop)
- These should open a triage ticket with recommended first checks:
  - model rollout status / route pinning
  - routing policy / region shift
  - cache config flags (enable/disable per route)

Paging vs ticketing guidance (draft)
- Page only if we believe there is immediate user-visible latency/cost impact AND it’s not a telemetry artifact.
- “User impact proxies” we can use without per-tenant cardinality:
  - p95 prefill latency increase correlated with cache misses (from traces, not labels)
  - overall token cost per completion rising (if available in aggregates)
- Otherwise, file tickets to Runtime/Platform teams with dashboards attached.

Reducing false positives: practical rules
1) Always alert on slices, not global
- Global hit-rate is mostly workload mix. Use (region, deployment_mode, model family, prompt_len_bucket) at minimum.

2) Keep an allowlist for high-value routes (page candidates)
- For Hosted: a curated allowlist of “tier-0” routes (internal + largest customers) maintained by SRE/Support.
- For Dedicated: page candidate by default (single tenant), but only if traffic gate is met.

3) Apply “burn-in” and change windows
- During known rollouts (new runtime build, telemetry config changes), suppress page-level cache regression alerts for 60–90 minutes.
- Use release annotations from Connor’s rollout plan to auto-silence.

4) Use multi-window confirmation
- e.g., require both 5m and 30m windows to breach threshold to reduce flaps.

5) Avoid per-tenant labels in alerts
- Do not page on “tenant_id” breakdown. Use internal analytics/drilldowns for tenant follow-up.

Expected diurnal patterns (notes for oncall)
- Hosted US-East:
  - 00:00–06:00 PT: more batch jobs; higher eviction pressure; hit-rate can dip in long prompt buckets.
  - 09:00–12:00 PT: chat/support traffic; more repeated system prompts; hit-rate tends to improve.
- EU regions:
  - Similar pattern shifted ~8–9 hours.
- Dedicated:
  - Tenant-specific; diurnal patterns vary. Use baseline per deployment.

Tuning numbers (initial, conservative)
- Hit-rate regression threshold: 8–12 percentage points drop vs baseline over 30m (bucketed).
- Wasted prefill spike threshold: +10 pp vs baseline over 15–30m.
- Pressure threshold: >0.85 utilization for 15m (with wasted prefill confirmation).
- Telemetry missing: >95% drop across broad slices for >= 10m (with stable request volume).

Open questions / TODO
- Confirm exact metric names + units post renaming (see runtime naming reconciliation PR). Need to update alert rules after final metrics land.
- Decide whether we have a stable “model family” dimension in metrics (or if we must map model_version -> family in dashboards only).
- Need a canonical “request volume stable” signal that doesn’t share the same ingestion path as cache metrics (to avoid correlated failure).
- Evaluate whether to include trace-based signals in page criteria (low-cardinality tags only) — Allison to sync with Nadia.
- Add a small “impact score” for paging: (wasted_prefill_tokens * cost_per_token_estimate) + (prefill_latency_increase * traffic).

Notes from incidents / tickets
- SUP-3912 (cache hit-rate dropped after model update): root cause was miss_reason=version_mismatch after rollout. Action: add dedicated alert classifier for version_mismatch and point to rollout checklist (route pinning + model version join key).
- SUP-3927 (dashboard shows zero hits): ingestion cardinality guard dropped labels; global dashboards looked like total failure. Action: page on telemetry-missing; also add a “dropped_by_guard” counter to ingestion and alert on that.

Next steps (this week)
- Sergio to implement rule drafts in observability-pack (behind feature flag / disabled paging by default).
- Allison to add runbook section: “Is this real or telemetry missing?” with exact dashboard panels to check.
- Aisha to schedule 30m review with Sean + Logan after canary week to tighten thresholds based on observed variability.

Changelog
- 2025-03-06: initial notes from eng-sre thread on thresholds; added gating + baseline ideas.
- 2025-03-11: added telemetry-missing page rule; incorporated SUP-3912/SUP-3927 learnings.
- 2025-03-17: tightened eviction+wasted-prefill coupling; added rollout suppression guidance.
